question: Provide the legal basis for each major conclusion, including regulation number and relevant article/annex where possible.

Build 01.answer:
## 1. Short answer

The principal legal basis is **Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915**, especially **Article 3 and Annex I, Section 1.1**, which set maximum levels for aflatoxins in food. For dried figs, the applicable row depends in part on whether they are intended for ordinary consumption or for sorting or other physical treatment before consumption or use as an ingredient.

The detection of aflatoxin B1 alone does not establish that this consignment exceeds the applicable maximum: the measured concentration, the applicable product-use category, and the relevant aflatoxin results must be established. Import controls and required documents also depend on the **current** listing of dried figs from Türkiye under Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1793.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

- **Maximum levels and marketability:** Regulation (EU) 2023/915, **Article 3 and Annex I, Section 1.1**. The Annex sets levels for aflatoxin B1 and for the sum of aflatoxins B1, B2, G1 and G2. Its dried-fig entries distinguish figs from those intended to undergo sorting or other physical treatment. The applicable entry and any associated conditions should be checked against the product’s actual intended use and the current consolidated Annex.
- **Food-business-operator responsibilities:** Regulation (EC) No 178/2002, **Article 17** (operator responsibility), **Article 14** (unsafe food), and **Article 19** (withdrawal and notification where applicable). These provisions do not, by themselves, establish that this particular consignment is non-compliant; that depends on the evidence and applicable maximum level.
- **Official controls and action on a non-compliant consignment:** Regulation (EU) 2017/625, particularly **Article 47** (official controls on certain goods entering the Union), **Articles 56–57** (CHED and related entry-control arrangements), and **Article 66** (measures concerning non-compliant consignments). The appropriate measure is for the competent authority to determine under the circumstances; detection alone does not establish which measure will be ordered.
- **Türkiye-specific import controls:** Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, particularly **Article 1 and Annexes I and II**. Those Annexes identify foods subject to increased official controls or special conditions, including any applicable control frequency and documentary conditions. The current consolidated listing must be checked before stating that a particular certificate, laboratory result, or control frequency applies.
- **Sampling and analysis:** Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/2782 lays down methods of sampling and analysis for the official control of mycotoxins. Whether a result establishes non-compliance depends on the applicable sampling and analytical rules as well as the reported result.

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

- The actual **aflatoxin B1 concentration**, the results for the other aflatoxins needed to assess the total, and whether the sampling and analysis were conducted under the applicable official-control rules.
- Whether the figs are intended for ordinary consumption or are genuinely intended for sorting or other physical treatment, and whether any conditions attached to that category are met.
- The **current** status of dried figs originating in Türkiye under Regulation (EU) 2019/1793 on the relevant date. Because the Annexes can change, do not infer a present certificate, analytical-report, notification, or inspection-frequency requirement without checking the version in force.
- Any shipment-specific facts—such as its presentation, intended destination or use, and official-control findings—that could affect the applicable category or action.

Build 03-B.answer:
## 1. Short answer

The fact that aflatoxin B1 was detected does **not by itself establish that the figs are non-compliant**: the concentration and the applicable product classification are not stated. For dried figs, Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Annex I, Table 1, row 1.1.3 sets a maximum level of **6.0 μg/kg for aflatoxin B1** and **10.0 μg/kg for the sum of aflatoxins**. Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Article 2, prohibits placing food covered by the Annex on the market when it exceeds the applicable maximum level.

The import-control rules are a separate issue. The frozen-corpus entry for dried figs from Türkiye is in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, Annex II, Section 1, row 14, with a **30% identity and physical check frequency**. That entry also entails consignment documentation requirements under Articles 10 and 11. Whether the shipment falls within that entry depends on its product/CN classification.

## 2. Legal basis and relevant conditions

- **Contaminant limit:** Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Annex I, Table 1, row **1.1.3** (“Dried figs”) gives the aflatoxin B1 and total-aflatoxin levels above. The row’s remark extends those levels to food consisting of dried figs as its only ingredient and to processed products consisting of at least 80% dried figs; for other products, Article 3(1) and (2) govern. The classification and any processing or ingredient composition therefore matter. The general market prohibition is in Article 2.
- **Import controls:** Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, Article 7 and Annex II, Section 1, row **14**, cover the listed Türkiye dried-fig products by the specified CN/TARIC classifications. Article 8 provides for identity and physical checks, including sampling and laboratory analysis, at the frequency stated in Annex II. The corpus entry reports 30% for the dried-fig row; that is a control frequency, not a finding about this particular consignment.
- **Accompanying documents:** For Annex II consignments, Regulation (EU) 2019/1793, Article 10 requires results of sampling and analyses performed by the relevant third-country competent authority; Article 11 requires an official certificate. Article 4 requires a duly finalised CHED before release for free circulation. These requirements depend on the consignment being within the relevant Annex II product classification.
- **Responsible actors and possible action:** Under Regulation (EC) No 178/2002, Article 17, food business operators must ensure compliance within their activities. Article 14 prohibits placing unsafe food on the market. If an operator has reason to believe food already placed on the market is not compliant with food-safety requirements, Article 19 sets out withdrawal, notification and, where necessary, consumer-recall duties. For official enforcement, Regulation (EU) 2017/625, Articles 65 and 138, address suspected and established non-compliance respectively; the measures taken depend on the competent authority’s findings.

## 3. Uncertainties / verification needed

The stated facts do not give the measured B1 concentration, the total-aflatoxin result, the analytical basis, the precise CN/TARIC classification, or whether the figs are sold as dried figs or incorporated into a processed product. Without those facts, neither a violation of the maximum level nor the precise import-control treatment can be concluded.

These are metadata observations, not verification that each cited provision is currently effective as applicable to this shipment. Before relying on them, check amendments, entry into force and application dates, transitional rules, Annex changes, and product-specific classification.

The traceability of food, feed, food-producing animals, and any other substance intended to be, or expected to be, incorporated into a food or feed shall be established at all stages of production, processing and distribution. 2. evidence.location: Article 19 — Responsibilities for food: food business operators
evidence.text: Article 19 Responsibilities for food: food business operators 1. If a food business operator considers or has reason to believe that a food which it has imported, produced, processed, manufactured or distributed is not in compliance with the food safety requirements, it shall immediately initiate procedures to withdraw the food in question from the market where the food has left the immediate control of that initial food business operator and inform the competent authorities thereof. Where the product may have reached the consumer, the operator shall effectively and accurately inform the consumers of the reason for its withdrawal, and if necessary, recall from consumers products already supplied to them when other measures are not sufficient to achieve a high level of health protection. 2. A food business operator responsible for retail or distribution activities which do not affect the packaging, labelling, safety or integrity of the food shall, within the limits of its respective activities, initiate procedures to withdraw from the market products not in compliance with the food-safety requirements and shall participate in contributing to the safety of the food by passing on relevant information necessary to trace a food, cooperating in the action taken by producers, processors, manufacturers and/or the competent authorities. 3. A food business operator shall immediately inform the competent authorities if it considers or has reason to believe that a food which it has placed on the market may be injurious to human health. Operators shall inform the competent authorities of the action taken to prevent risks to the final consumer and shall not prevent or discourage any person from cooperating, in accordance with national law and legal practice, with the competent

fe, unless following a detailed assessment there is no evidence that the rest of the batch, lot or consignment is unsafe. 7. Food that complies with specific Community provisions governing food safety shall be deemed to be safe insofar as the aspects covered by the specific Community provisions are concerned. 8. Conformity of a food with specific provisions applicable to that food shall not bar the competent authorities from taking appropriate measures to impose restrictions on it being placed on the market or to require its withdrawal from the market where there are reasons to suspect that, despite such conformity, the food is unsafe. 9. Where there are no specific Community provisions, food shall be deemed to be safe when it conforms to the specific provisions of national food law of the Member State in whose territory the food is marketed, such provisions being drawn up and applied without prejudice to the Treaty, in particular Articles 28 and 30 thereof.

evidence.text: Article 20 Responsibilities for feed: feed business operators 1. If a feed business operator considers or has reason to believe that a feed which it has imported, produced, processed, manufactured or distributed does not satisfy the feed safety requirements, it shall immediately initiate procedures to withdraw the feed in question from the market and inform the competent authorities thereof. In these circumstances or, in the case of Article 15(3), where the batch, lot or consignment does not satisfy the feed safety requirement, that feed shall be destroyed, unless the competent authority is satisfied otherwise. The operator shall effectively and accurately inform users of the feed of the reason for its withdrawal, and if necessary, recall from them products already supplied when other measures are not sufficient to achieve a high level of health protection. 2. A feed business operator shall immediately inform the competent authorities if it considers or has reason to believe that a feed which it placed on the market may not satisfy the feed safety requirements. Article 3 Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions apply: (1) ‘food law’ means food law as defined in point (1) of Article 3 of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002; (2) ‘feed law’ means the laws, regulations and administrative provisions governing feed in general and feed safety in particular, whether at Union or national level at any stage of production, processing and distribution or use of feed; (3) ‘competent authorities’ means: (a) the central authorities of a Member State responsible for the organisation of official controls and of other official activities, in accordance with this Regulation and the rules referred to in Article 1(2); (b) any other authority to which that responsibility has been conferred; (c) where appropriate, the corresponding authorities of a third country; (4) ‘organic control authority’ means a public administrative organisation for organic production and labelling of organic products of a Member State to which the competent authorities have conferred, in whole or in part, their competences in relation to the application of Council Regulation (EC) No 834/2007 ( 3 ), including, where appropriate, the corresponding authority of a third country or operating in a third country; (5) ‘delegated body’ means a separate legal person to which the competent authorities have delegated certain official control tasks or certain tasks related to other official activities; (6) ‘control verification procedures’ means the arrangements put in place and actions performed by the competent authorities for the purpose of ensuring that official controls and other official activities are consistent and effective; (7) ‘control system’ means a system comprising the competent authorities and the resources, structures, arrangements and

Article 14 Food safety requirements 1. Food shall not be placed on the market if it is unsafe. 2. Food shall be deemed to be unsafe if it is considered to be: (a) injurious to health; (b) unfit for human consumption. 3. In determining whether any food is unsafe, regard shall be had: (a) to the normal conditions of use of the food by the consumer and at each stage of production, processing and distribution, and (b) to the information provided to the consumer, including information on the label, or other information generally available to the consumer concerning the avoidance of specific adverse health effects from a particular food or category of foods. 4. In determining whether any food is injurious to health, regard shall be had: (a) not only to the probable immediate and/or short-term and/or long-term effects of that food on the health of a person consuming it, but also on subsequent generations; (b) to the probable cumulative toxic effects; (c) to the particular health sensitivities of a specific category of consumers where the food is intended for that category of consumers. 5. In determining whether any food is unfit for human consumption, regard shall be had to whether the food is unacceptable for human consumption according to its intended use, for reasons of contamination, whether by extraneous matter or otherwise, or through putrefaction, deterioration or decay. 6. Where any food which is unsafe is part of a batch, lot or consignment of food of the same class or description, it shall be presumed that all the food in that batch, lot or consignment is also unsafe, unless following a detailed assessment there is no evidence that the rest of the batch, lot or consignment is unsafe. 7. If groundnuts (peanuts) and other oilseeds with inedible shell are analysed, it is assumed when calculating the aflatoxin content that all the contamination is on the edible part. In the case of food consisting of groundnuts (peanuts) and other oilseeds used as only ingredient or in the case of processed products consisting at least of 80 % from the groundnuts (peanuts) and other oilseeds concerned, the maximum levels as established for the corresponding groundnuts (peanuts) and other oilseeds apply also to those products. In other cases, Articles 3(1) and (2) apply.

ANNEX II
